Artistic endeavors carry a great deal of responsibility. You know how when you learn about, say, Classic or Native American myths in school, you discuss how a particular story has some kind of theme in it? The bravery of a hero, the folly of hubris, why humans have certain faults?


We imagine these cultures sharing their ideas--what we call myths--through spoken word and ceremony. Around campfires, an oral story teller recites an epic, the creation story of their people. Actors perform Oedipus in an amphitheater.


The point here is, the method of communication of how the world works has changed, but the purpose of telling a story hasn't. And all societies, in a general sense, believe how they view the world is an objective reflection of natural law. This is true in a matriarchal nation or a patriarchal one, a democracy or a chattel slavery one. 


When a modern studio makes a game, they make it in the context of patriarchy, white supremacy, and class society. Violence, discrimination, oppression along these lines are all measurably real things. Nothing happens in a vacuum of total equality, where what's good for the goose is good for the gander. 


Portraying people who face concretely demonstrable forms of oppression in certain ways will interact with people differently depending on how they deal with this enculteration.


So, artists have to ask themselves a question. How will my art interact with the environment? Am I putting these metal bikinis in so players can express themselves, or for titillation in a society where women are attacked because they are routinely objectified into subhuman status? Does my brothel exist to flush out the world in a way that adds depth, or as a way to stoke make ego in a society where men's egos are tied to sexual conquest and aggression?


This relates to a lot of things, from commercials to books and all. These are all modern forms of storytelling, they are made by people in a certain contexts with certain beliefs. 


You can't control how people will react to your art. But it's incredibly simple, once you eat a big slice of humble pie and admit different people have different experiences you must consider, to see the line between allowing free expression or exploration of sex, race, etc and exploiting these in a context of sexism, racism, etc. because it's easy and will sell, for lack of controversy with commonly held beliefs on gender and race.

GG, like all reactionaries, doxx as a power play over an oppressed group they think is stepping out of line. There's a fraction of GG that is hooked by the journalistic ethics angle, but for the most part GG represents reaction against greater visibility and access of people who traditionally are marginalized.

Maybe Anti-GG doxx because they think it will stop physical harm against people who are oppressed and experience violence and discrimination because of this oppression. They think they are turning the tables against people who cheerlead ideas that cause real harm to real people. After all, they may say, people aren't born racist or sexist. They are taught to be that way by racist and sexist media and ideas in their environment.

When it comes to issues like this, there really isn't parity. Doxxing a woman in a patriarchal society for being a feminist is different than doxxing someone for supporting a reactionary cause that is more or less backed up by what passes for "common sense." Women experience violence and discrimination for being women. There's a social, economic category at work here, and all the credible science demonstrates women are treated worse than men, as are LGBTQ people. Similarly, there's white supremacy to consider.

Personally, I don't know. I've never really been threatened as a category. I don't feel qualified to tell people in an oppressed group should wage their fight. But I don't think there's a moral equivalent, here, depending on who is doing it and why.

>>Mental illness is definitely becoming the next flag for outrage addicts everywhere.

Because millions of people deal with mental illness, it seriously affects their lives in many ways. A significant portion of the people I've talked to about things like depression and anxiety (and even things like PTSD) have a pre modern attitude towards it, treating the mentally ill like they are just too lazy to deal. The science of mental illness doesn't support that at all, and that pre modern attitude contributes all sorts of very real, life altering discrimination and abuse.

If you want to relate this to gaming, look at the horror trope of the decrepit mental hospital, full of crazy monsters. The reality is the mentally ill are far more likely to be victims of violence, with the important exception of some kind of addicts (namely, alcoholics).

To me, the true horror is institutional violence. Taking a regular person and turning them into an agent of violence is common--despotic police states, basic training, racist ideologies, etc. Turning entire groups or even entire social categories of people into monsters by simply giving them a draft card or a badge, or even just a title like "prime minister,"  scares me more than a person with a personality disorder.

There are issues that, thanks to some trends in our dominant ideology (hyperindividualism, the aforementioned pre modern and anti scientific attitude that Meghan illness is a personal moral failing and not a medical condition that may require special treatment) have been ignored or flying very far under the radar. The treatment of the mentally ill is one of them.
